## BLOCKING — B1: g7/g8 probe-FAILURE disposition unspecified (fail-open)

D4 keys g7/g8 on probe OUTPUT, never on probe FAILURE. A non-zero rc from
`git status --porcelain` / `git worktree list --porcelain` (corrupt or
half-removed tree, damaged `.git` pointer, unreadable index) yields empty
stdout, which a naive implementation reads as "zero rows ⇒ clean" — and the
tree then flows into `cleanup_branch_src`, whose body is UNCONDITIONALLY
destructive past the gate: `worktree remove --force`, then
`shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)` REGARDLESS of the remove's
outcome, then `prune` (slurm.py:3863-3880). That destroys a tree whose
reproducibility was never verified — the K1 class, and a violation of the
body's positive-verified-evidence contract (disk-hygiene.md #2127: probe
failure ⇒ KEEP, "refuse rather than inflict").

Survives the planned suite: T1-T8 all use HEALTHY fixtures, so a fail-open
implementation passes every test AND the §6 dry-run (all 13 live trees healthy).

Required: one D4 sentence — any git probe failure (non-zero rc at g7 or g8, at
classification OR re-probe) ⇒ `kept — probe failed` + escalate, never treated
as clean — plus a T-case with a corrupted `.git` pointer asserting KEPT.
Also make `locked` an explicit base-gate keep: on git 2.34 a locked worktree
refuses single-`--force` removal, the rmtree still destroys the dir, and
`prune` skips locked registrations — leaving a stale registration that makes
the next `materialize_branch_src` `worktree add` FAIL, wedging that issue's
SLURM lane. (0 of 13 live registrations are locked today — spec hole, not a
live hazard. Independently re-confirmed by the orchestrator.)

- S1 (premise D): the planned disk-hygiene.md paragraph must EXPLICITLY

  reads "repo-root OR worktrees" and the scratch IS a registered worktree — by
  stating the clean-tree condition as the reproducibility proof. Folds into the
  existing D7/§4 doc edit; no new work.
- S2 (premise E): §2 hand-verified cleanliness on only 3/13 sampled, but §6

## ALTERNATIVES — A1 (concern, not blocking): file the sparse follow-up now

The critic found, and the orchestrator independently confirmed, that
`RSYNC_INCLUDE_PATHS` (slurm.py) carries NO `eval_results` entry — the include
set is pyproject/uv.lock/src/scripts/configs/external-open-instruct/tests/

keeps the eval-result history + dashboards out of scratch". So the 7.8 GB

A sparse-checkout scratch would cut ~80%+ of the footprint AT THE SOURCE and
cut per-dispatch materialization cost. It does NOT replace the tier (accretion
is unbounded in issue count; killed launchers still leak whatever is
materialized), so janitor-first / sparse-follow-up is the right ordering — but

- A (D2 gate sufficiency): HOLDS except B1. Fixture-tested on this VM's git

## The two reviewers were each HALF right — verified by live reproduction

Claude graded this area MINOR (`porcelain-newline-parse-ambiguity`, deferred
by the orchestrator in `epm:progress v9` on the ground that no such path
exists on this host). Codex graded the same area CRITICAL but attributed it to
C-QUOTING. Both attributions were tested directly on git 2.34.1
(`/tmp/qtest`, six adversarial worktree paths):

| path contains | porcelain emission | parser outcome |
|---|---|---|
| space | RAW (`/tmp/qtest/we ird`) | correct |
| tab | RAW (literal `\t`) | correct |
| backslash | RAW (`/tmp/qtest/back\slash`) | correct |
| double quote | RAW (`/tmp/qtest/qu"ote`) | correct |
| **newline** | **`worktree /tmp/qtest/nl` + orphan line `line`** | **WRONG** |

- **Codex's stated mechanism is DISPROVEN.** git 2.34.1 does not C-quote
  worktree paths in `--porcelain`; every special character except newline is
  emitted raw. `-z` is unavailable on this version (confirmed).
- **Codex's SEVERITY is CORRECT, via newline truncation.** Reproduced end to
  end: the parser records the truncated `/tmp/qtest/nl`; the real registered
  path `/tmp/qtest/nl<LF>line`, which exists on disk, is ABSENT from the set;
  the positive registration proof therefore compares unequal, the candidate is
  judged UNREGISTERED, and it reaches `shutil.rmtree`. Fail-OPEN in a deletion
  gate — destroying a registered worktree without unregistering it. SIB-1 is
  the same defect reached through gate-1.7 branch (c).
- The orphan continuation line also feeds the g1 regex: a worktree named
  `issue-<digits><LF>...` truncates to a string matching `^issue-(\d+)$` and is
  admitted as a valid issue tree.

**Why the correction is load-bearing, not pedantry:** implementing the fix as
Codex described it — decode C-quoting — would be DEAD CODE on this git version
AND would leave the actual hole wide open. The severity is adopted; the
mechanism is replaced with the reproduced one.

## Round 4 scope (single root cause, single fix)

Parse `git worktree list --porcelain` in RECORD form and FAIL CLOSED on
ambiguity: any non-blank line that is not a recognized porcelain key
(`worktree `, `HEAD `, `branch `, `detached`, `bare`, `locked`, `prunable`)
is an unparseable continuation ⇒ the listing is AMBIGUOUS ⇒ return `None`.
Callers already treat `None` as refuse-to-reap (verified by both reviewers at
:2052-2056), so the fail-closed path is already wired. Drop the `.strip()`,
which corrupts trailing-space paths.

This one fix closes R3-C1, SIB-1, and the Claude minor together — they were
always the same defect. My round-3 deferral of it was the wrong call, and the
reproduction is what settled it.

## What round 4 fixed, and what it did not

Round 4 (`86b1355140`, `e591e5dc1f`) rewrote `_registered_worktree_paths` as a
record-form parse that fails CLOSED on unrecognized lines, dropped the
path-corrupting `.strip()`, and added 5 regression tests. Its end-to-end
pre-fix test is the strongest evidence produced in this task: the boobytrap
FIRED, i.e. `shutil.rmtree` was actually reached on a reap-eligible candidate
under an ambiguous listing — the R3-C1 data-loss shape demonstrated rather
than argued. 84/84 new-suite, 212 passed across the janitor suites, K3
tier-(f) parity intact, sidecar delta 0.

The implementer disclosed a residual and characterized it as
"adversarial-only, **not producible by real git output**". That
characterization is FALSE, verified by reproduction.

## Reproduction (real git 2.34.1, isolated repo, no adversary)

A worktree whose path contains a newline followed by a bare porcelain keyword:

```
$ git -C /tmp/qtest2/main worktree add --detach "$(printf '/tmp/qtest2/sp\nbare')"
$ git -C /tmp/qtest2/main worktree list --porcelain
worktree /tmp/qtest2/main
HEAD 9d190ff0...
branch refs/heads/main

worktree /tmp/qtest2/sp
bare
HEAD 9d190ff0...
detached
```

Against the round-4 parser at `e591e5dc1f`:

```
_registered_worktree_paths('/tmp/qtest2/main')
  -> {'/tmp/qtest2/main', '/tmp/qtest2/sp'}   # a SET, not None
  '/tmp/qtest2/sp\nbare' exists on disk : True
  '/tmp/qtest2/sp\nbare' in the set     : False
```

The registered worktree is absent from the proof set ⇒ judged UNREGISTERED ⇒
reaches `shutil.rmtree`. Same fail-open class as R3-C1, still open. The
`bare` + `detached` coexistence does not trip the round-4 slot-uniqueness
rules, because a genuine record simply lacks `bare`.

**Methodological note:** my FIRST run of this probe returned `None` and looked
safe. It was CONFOUNDED — the earlier `nl<LF>line` worktree was still
registered in that repo and forced `None` on its own. The isolated repo above
is the clean measurement. Recorded because the confounded result would have
closed this as a non-issue.

## Disposition — folded in at zero review cost

The round-4 review ensemble has NOT yet been dispatched, so this fix lands in
the same implementation round and the ensemble reviews the complete diff. No
review round is consumed.

Prescribed fix: every parsed `worktree` path must exist on disk as a
directory; a parsed path that does not exist is tolerated ONLY when its own
record carries `prunable` (the one legitimate missing-directory case — without
that carve-out a routinely pruned worktree would wedge the whole tier);
otherwise the listing is AMBIGUOUS ⇒ `None`. This catches the spoof exactly:
`/tmp/qtest2/sp` does not exist; only `/tmp/qtest2/sp<LF>bare` does.

Residual (b) — `scripts/verify_task_body.py:6955` and
`scripts/audit_stranded_task_commits.py:43` share the latent line-wise pattern
— stays UNTOUCHED and disclosed: both are read-only and license no deletion,
and widening scope mid-revision-round is the wrong move. Recorded here so it
is visible to the reviewers rather than buried in an agent memory file.
